Independent bounded secular root and odd-row residual calculation
correctness.rationale: For the reflecting mean-field ODE in Cao–Gong's time normalization, the only mean-feedback derivative is mₕ(eₖ−e₋ₖ)/[k(2k+1)]. The even mass-zero sector is strictly decaying. On the odd sector let A be minus the reflecting generator with a Dirichlet value at zero. Solving its endpoint forcing gives A⁻¹eₖ=2(1,…,k)ᵀ. Conjugation by A⁻¹/² makes the odd Jacobian a symmetric rank-one perturbation of −A; the inertia criterion is 4Σj²/[k(2k+1)]=2(k+1)/3>1, so there is one positive and no zero tangent eigenvalue. The positive eigenfunction is proportional to sinh(jt), where λ=cosh(t)−1; the reflecting endpoint equation gives precisely the displayed unique strictly positive root. The trivial t=0 of the unnormalized equation is not an eigenmode. At k=1 the direct odd Jacobian is −1/2+2/3=1/6. Multiplying the second difference of sinh(jt) by j and telescoping gives the stated finite-sum identity and λₖ=2(1−Rₖ)/(2k+1). The bound λₖ<2/(2k+1) gives tₖ→0. Bounded ktₖ along a subsequence would make the secular left side O(tₖ) and the right side at least 2(k+1)tₖ/3, a contradiction. Hence coth(ktₖ)→1, Rₖ∼1/(ktₖ), tₖ∼√(2/k), and √k(1−kλₖ)→1/√2, with the correct minus sign in λₖ. The sinh quotient at distance floor(x√k) from k tends to exp(−√2 x) for each fixed x≥0. A fresh bounded bisection/residual check for k=1,8,64 had maximum normalized odd eigenvector residuals below 9×10⁻¹⁶; at k=6400 the scaled eigenvalue correction was −0.710238689 and profile at x=1 was 0.244655614, compared with limits −0.707106781 and 0.243116734.
residual_risks: The bounded numerical tests do not prove the limit. The proof establishes the pointwise profile of the single unstable eigenmode; it does not establish nonlinear or stochastic escape rates.

value.rationale: For an existing opinion model, knowing that an instability exists does not tell how its linear timescale or the opinions carrying the mode change as the opinion scale grows. The growth law supplies a linear e-folding time of order k with a definite next correction, while the normalized eigenvector confines the growth mode to an endpoint distance of order √k instead of the full O(k) span. These are complementary and structurally useful quantitative answers to a gap left by the index and symmetric-mode results.
residual_risks: No assertion about nonlinear basin selection, generic nonlinear escape time, or finite-agent fluctuations should be inferred from these local spectral data.
